question.prompt: A running track is the ring formed by two concentric circles. It is \(10\) feet wide. The circumferences of the two circles differ by about:

solutions.explanation:
The track's width is the difference between the two radii. Let the inner radius be \(r>0\) feet, so the outer radius is \(r+10\) feet. Using \(C=2\pi r\), the circumference difference is
\[
2\pi(r+10)-2\pi r=20\pi\text{ feet}.
\]
The unknown inner radius cancels, so the width alone determines the difference. Since \(20\pi\approx62.8\), the best listed approximation is 60 feet, choice C.
solutions.title: Use the difference between the radii
